item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00436","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C22","C21","C24"],"selected_candidate_label":"C22","confidence":0.67,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C22 plausibly supplied a concrete personnel-procedure component: acquisition of civil-service status through a suitable noncompetitive examination prescribed by the Civil Service Commission. The child generalizes that same Commission-controlled noncompetitive-examination mechanism for defense hiring, while contrasting it with competitive registers. C21 contains nearly identical machinery but is earlier and less closely aligned in timing; C24 is relevant mainly to the child's reemployment provision. The overlap is narrower than a full-document template but material enough to qualify.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the Commission should, for such time as it deems necessary, authorize noncompetitive examination procedures, subject to such limitations and minimum recruitment standards as the Commission may prescribe","parent_excerpt":"The employee must successfully qualify in such suitable noncompetitive examination as the Civil Service Commission may prescribe","explanation":"Both assign the Civil Service Commission authority to prescribe and administer noncompetitive examination procedures."},{"child_excerpt":"The release of employees from permanent positions for employment in national defense activities and their subsequent reemployment in permanent positions... should be governed by a single set of standards and conditions","parent_excerpt":"any employee of the Federal Government without competitive status... shall be entitled to and shall acquire a competitive status upon compliance with the following conditions","explanation":"Both use centrally specified civil-service conditions to regularize federal employees' status, although the child's reemployment rule is a distinct adaptation."}]}
